subject: Re: PayGrid model fit eval - parity thresholds and next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>
To: Carlos Rivera <carlos.rivera@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-20T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: PayGrid model fit eval - post-demo recap and next steps

Hi Carlos —

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) What we heard
- Key goal: replace current proprietary rerank + LLM pipeline with an open-model-backed solution while maintaining parity on intent accuracy and reranking MRR.
- Acceptance criteria you mentioned: minimal user-facing regressions and measurable parity on our benchmark QA set (you suggested >98% intent match / <2% drop in MRR).

2) Redwood recommended shortlist (to run in our eval harness):
- small-open-v1-quantized (latency-optimized) — recommended for early latency tests
- opt-neo-rl-3b (strong baseline for QA)
- redwood-rl-4b (proprietary baseline we can tune)

3) Deliverables we'll send by Friday:
- parity benchmark CSV (sample metrics and per-query diffs)
- canonical prompt set for your QA/eval team (prompt-set-paygrid-v1.txt)
- runbook for running the calibration harness and KV caching recommendations

4) Next steps / asks for PayGrid:
- Please confirm the acceptance thresholds in writing (intent accuracy, rerank MRR targets).
- Share the canonical QA dataset (or an anonymized subset) for us to ingest into the eval harness. If you prefer, we can run only on our side with data you provide via S3/Drive.
- Confirm availability for a 30-min calibration run the week of 5/24 so we can sync results and recommended quant configs.

Attaching an initial parity benchmark export and the prompt set for your review. Links to the full report and the HubSpot deal are below.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.inference

Attachments: paygrid-parity-benchmarks-v1.csv; prompt-set-paygrid-v1.txt
From: Carlos Rivera <carlos.rivera@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ana Lopez <ana.lopez@paygrid.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PayGrid model fit eval - parity thresholds and next steps

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the fast follow-up and the materials. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Acceptance thresholds: informally we said ~98% intent accuracy but to be explicit we need:
  * Intent classification accuracy >= 98% on our holdout set (weighted by query volume)
  * Rerank MRR drop <= 1.5% relative to current production
  * Latency P95 for the top-level request <= 350ms (including network hops)

- We'll share a 10k-query anonymized subset by EOD Monday (5/24) via our secured S3 link.
- Can Redwood also provide an A/B configuration we can run in staging (simple traffic split) to validate user metrics once we hit parity in the harness?

One concern from our ML team: we worry about subtle quality regressions (e.g., hallucination leading to incorrect entity extraction) even if higher-level intent accuracy looks okay. Can you outline how Redwood detects and alerts on quality regressions post-rollout?

Happy to do the 30-min calibration run week of 5/24 — mornings PST are best.

—Carlos
Carlos Rivera
Head of Product, PayGrid
carlos.rivera@paygrid.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Carlos Rivera <carlos.rivera@paygrid.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-05-25T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PayGrid model fit eval - parity thresholds and next steps

Hi Carlos — thanks for the clear thresholds and for sharing the subset. Short plan to address the items and the quality-regression concern: 

1) Eval plan (what we'll run this week)- Calibration run (5/25 morning PST): run the three shortlisted variants across your 10k anonymized queries with per-query diffs and answer overlap metrics.
- Metrics we'll surface: intent accuracy, top-1 answer F1, MRR, latency P50/P95, hallucination score (heuristic-based flagging), and confidence distribution by intent.

2) Parity gating and acceptance- We'll produce a parity report with pass/fail per-threshold you listed. Pass requires meeting all three thresholds. For borderline cases we will annotate queries with behavioral diffs and proposed prompt/temperature adjustments.

3) Post-rollout quality monitoring- Redwood Console provides:
  * Per-route token-level cost & latency breakdowns (already in Console)
  * Quality monitors: we'll wire your canonical prompt/eval set as a regression suite that runs nightly on a mirror of sampled traffic; any drop (you can set a 0.5% or 1% guardrail) triggers an alert and opens a rollback playbook.
  * Sampled output retention (configurable) and quick diff viewer for triage.

4) Action items- From Redwood: run calibration on 5/25 AM PST and send the parity report same day; if we hit parity we'll prepare an A/B staging config (simple 10/90 split) for you to run and observe user metrics.
- From PayGrid: share S3 link (please ensure read access for inference-team@redwood.inference) and confirm a 30-min slot 5/25 9:30am PST.

I'll start the calibration run as soon as we have the S3 link. Aditya — can you prewarm the quantized cluster and include the quant config we used for the latency runs?

Thanks — looking forward to the calibration.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Product Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference

Attachments referenced: runbook-calibration.md (link in Drive), paygrid-parity-benchmarks-v1.csv
